memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'No one, however, may dedicate the firstborn of an animal, since the
firstborn already belongs to the LORD; whether an ox or a sheep, it is
the LORD's. If it is one of the unclean animals, it may be bought back at
its set value, adding a fifth of the value to it. If it is not redeemed,
it is to be sold at its set value'" - Lev 27:26-27 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
You could not dedicate the firstborn animal to God as though it were a
gift — because it was already His. Ever since the night of Passover in
Egypt, the firstborn belonged to the Lord. You cannot give someone what
already belongs to them.

This is a humbling correction to how we sometimes think about our giving.
We can imagine we are being generous with God, presenting Him with gifts,
when in truth everything we have was already His to begin with.

Dear friend, this reframes the whole idea of offering. We are not
benefactors doing God a favour. We are stewards returning to the Owner
what was always His. Our time, our abilities, our money, our very breath
— all of it belongs to Him first.

The psalmist says the earth is the LORD's, and everything in it (Ps 24:1).
Paul asks, what do you have that you did not receive? (1 Cor 4:7).

Far from diminishing our giving, this makes it richer. When we understand
that we own nothing absolutely, giving becomes an act of joyful
acknowledgment: "Lord, this was always Yours; I gladly return it to You."

And there is one more thought here. We ourselves, having been redeemed by
Christ, already belong to God. Paul says you are not your own; you were
bought at a price (1 Cor 6:19-20). The most fitting response is simply to
live as those who know they already belong to Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I give to God as a benefactor or as a steward returning His own?
2. Have I grasped that I myself already belong to God?
3. How does knowing I own nothing absolutely change my giving?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, everything is already Yours, including me. Help me give not as
one doing You a favour, but as a steward gladly returning what was always
Yours. Amen.
